recommendation: Keep the fix. It preserves the FHIR-25462 profile/supportedProfile distinction while aligning current core guidance with the later final deprecation decision for declared-profile, avoiding stale implementer guidance.
issue_request: FHIR-25462 was Published/Persuasive with Modification and asked for guidance around CapabilityStatement profile use, especially distinguishing resource.profile for system-wide expectations from supportedProfile/use-case-specific behavior and compatible profiling.html guidance.
initial_application: The seed was applied in 8fb57bffdcfcaef0a694269d3930aae57f3c35e5 by updating CapabilityStatement.rest.resource.profile and .supportedProfile definitions, adding declared-profile in core, and adding profiling.html guidance to use that extension. a2e0206d1d15324a318ed83dd5d55c65be16e584 later adjusted the .profile example wording from lowest-common-denominator to superset. The current CapabilityStatement source still contains the intended profile/supportedProfile split and is active in source/fhir.ini.
additional_context: The declared-profile extension was later moved to the FHIR Extension Pack. Published Extension Pack issue FHIR-40930 resolved to deprecate the extension because no one indicated use and to point users to CapabilityStatement.rest.resource.supportedProfile; Extension Pack source now marks the extension retired/deprecated with that reason. Zulip and Confluence evidence for FHIR-40930 show the same uncertainty about the distinction from supportedProfile and a final 10-0-0 FHIR-I vote.
reconciliation: Changed source/profiling.html so the relevant paragraph says producers communicate these use-case-specific profiles with CapabilityStatement.rest.resource.supportedProfile and notes that Declared Profile is deprecated and should not be used for this purpose in new CapabilityStatements. No structural CapabilityStatement elements were changed because they already reflected the applied seed decision.
source_changes: source/profiling.html: replaced the recommendation to use the Declared Profile extension with supportedProfile guidance and a deprecation warning for new CapabilityStatements.

related_jiras.note: Published Extension Pack issue that deprecated capabilitystatement-declared-profile and directed users to CapabilityStatement.rest.resource.supportedProfile. Used as controlling later context, not separately decided in core.
Published Extension Pack clarification of declared-profile wording before the later retirement; confirms the same guidance family but did not require a separate core decision.
